newsitem.title: PANAMA: Taiwanese envoy visits Panama, pledges funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwanese envoy visits Panama, pledges funds.

text.p: Taiwan's Foreign Minister John Chang arrived in Panama on Tuesday to meet with top government officials as part of a 22-day Central America tour to reaffirm the island's links with the region, the Foreign Ministry said.
Chang briefly broke away from his diplomatic meetings to tour the rundown Chinatown district in central Panama City and said Taiwan would donate funds to the city to help rebuild the district.
Chang had earlier met his Panamanian counterpart, Ricardo Arias, to exchange views over the handover of Hong Kong and explain Taipei's policies toward Beijing.
The 30 countries still with diplomatic relations with Taiwan have come under increasing pressure from China to break off friendly relations with the island.

Chang will meet President Ernesto Perez Balladares on Wednesday and visit the Colon free-trade zone -- the world's second largest after Hong Kong and an important transit point for Taiwanese goods, the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
Taiwan is also an important investor in Panama. Shipping giant Evergreen Marine has spent $200 million on a new port facility and has applied to set up its EVA Airways unit there.

The Taiwanese government has contributed $800,000 to help organize an international conference on the future of the Panama Canal in September and its President Lee Teng-hui has said he will attend the conference.
